Job gains have moderated but remain strong, and unemployment is low—signals of activity near potential. In New Keynesian frameworks with a hybrid Phillips curve (Galí and Gertler, 1999) and inflation-forecast targeting that anchors expectations (Svensson, 1997; Svensson and Woodford, 1999), such labor-market tightness need not reignite inflation if policy credibility is preserved, consistent with Friedman-Phelps’ view of no long-run trade-off. Maintaining the policy rate near 5.25–5.50% aligns with Taylor-rule guidance and acknowledges the welfare costs of above-target inflation (Lucas; Cooley and Hansen; Ireland), so the tone is cautiously positive rather than exuberant.
